test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which is the most important feature of federal government adopted by India?

options.text: The state government has more power than the union government.
The jurisdiction of all governments is the same.
The relationship between the state and the center should be based on cooperation.
The center is financially dependent on states.

solution:
The correct answer is "**The relationship between the state and the center should be based on cooperation**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India is a** federal system**,but leans towards a unitary system of government.
 
• It is sometimes considered a **quasi-federal system** because it has features of both **federal **and** unitary** systems.
 
• **Article 1** of the Indian Constitution states that "**India, meaning Bharat, is a federation of states."**
 
• The word **union** does not appear in the constitution.
 
• The federal element was introduced into modern India by the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• This law separated powers between central and local councils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Two levels of government,-center and state.
 
• Division of Powers Between Central and State - The 7th Schedule of the Constitution has three lists indicating the issues for which each level has jurisdiction: the union list, the state list and the concurrent list.
 
• The Constitution is the** supreme law **of India.
 
• The constitution provides for an independent and unified judiciary.
 
• The lower courts and district courts are at the lowest level and the Supreme Court is at the state level.
 
• The highest court is the Supreme Court of India. All courts are subordinate to the **Supreme Court.**
